subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should an oversized inbound IRC record be a fatal connection error under the existing supervisor, and should the limit account for IRCv3's separate message-tag allowance?
rationale: Source and real TCP proof establish the memory problem, but the repository does not establish whether strict RFC-style disconnects, bounded record discard, extended-tag interoperability, or reconnect suppression is the intended product contract.

options.title: Prove and constrain fail-close
options.body: Keep the fatal disconnect, add focused supervision/backoff proof, and enforce separate limits for the IRCv3 tag section and the traditional message portion when tags are supported.

options.title: Discard oversized records
options.body: Enter a bounded discard-until-newline state and report the protocol violation without tearing down an otherwise usable connection.

options.title: Accept the strict boundary
options.body: Merge the current behavior while explicitly accepting that oversized or extended tagged records may disconnect and subsequently reconnect the account.

recommendation.title: Prove and constrain fail-close
recommendation.body: Keep the fatal disconnect, add focused supervision/backoff proof, and enforce separate limits for the IRCv3 tag section and the traditional message portion when tags are supported.

likelyOwner.reason: The IRC feature-introduction history makes this person the best available owner for the channel's protocol and reconnection contract.
